Anna (Security): Heads-up — we're planning RBAC privilege pruning for keystore service accounts tomorrow 2026-03-25 09:00 UTC. This will remove broad kms:Decrypt rights from legacy SAs and replace with scoped key alias grants. Please review now and update runbooks.
Mike (Infra): timeline? any expected mTLS/handshake impact?
Anna (Security): Timeline: canary in europe-west1 at t0 (09:00 UTC), then 10% increments per region. Expect brief KMS Deny entries if a service still references old SA. We'll gate by handshake_err_pct on the /mtls/handshake metric.
Jess (SRE): Can we gate automatically? last time we saw a 0.9% spike and it paged.
Anna (Security): Yes — plan is: pause if handshake_err_pct > 0.5% for Canary sustained >5m. Canary nodes are labeled proxy-keystore-canary-*. We'll also enable tighter audit sampling during the rollout.
Ralph (Dev): Quick check — how do I find those Deny logs if I need to investigate?
Anna (Security): Use this logging query (GCP) — should find decrypt denies and SA in the payload:

```
resource.type="k8s_container"
logName="projects/redwood-prod/logs/keystore-audit"
jsonPayload.event="kms:DecryptDenied"
jsonPayload.serviceAccount: "proxy-keystore"
```

or run:

```
gcloud logging read 'logName="projects/redwood-prod/logs/keystore-audit" AND jsonPayload.event="kms:DecryptDenied"' --limit 50 --freshness=1h
```

That will show the audit entries and the member that got denied.
SRE-Bot: alert created: keystore.kms.decrypt_denied > 10 in 5m -> slack @oncall
Priya (Oncall): I'm already seeing a small spike in the eu-west canary at 08:54 UTC: 12 decrypt_denied entries; handshake_err 0.6% over 3m.
Anna (Security): Thanks — immediate mitigation path: add a temporary scoped binding allowing decrypt for the canary SA only while we remediate services. We should avoid broad grants. Example GCP command below.
Omar (DevOps): Is this GCP KMS or AWS KMS for that cluster? We have mixed infra.
Anna (Security): This cluster uses GCP KMS keyring `keystore-prod` in europe-west1. For GCP the quick mitigation is:

```
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding keystore-key \
  --location=europe-west1 \
  --keyring=keystore-prod \
  --member="serviceAccount:proxy-keystore-canary@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
  --role="roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter"
```

Make it time-limited and record the audit link. We will rotate back to scoped aliases as soon as services are patched.
Jess (SRE): Also push a patch to proxy to retry with exponential backoff and use cached prefix fallback for 30s while IAM stabilizes.
Ralph (Dev): I'll scan the codebase for hardcoded SA names and old key aliases. Quick grep:

```
rg "proxy-keystore@|keystore-prod-key" || true
```

I'll post results.
Priya (Oncall): I'll update the runbook with exact rollback commands, the gcloud snippet, and the watch conditions (pause if handshake_err_pct > 0.5% for >5m). Will also add a link to the audit logs query.
Anna (Security): Sample audit log line we saw earlier (sanitized):

```
{"timestamp":"2026-03-25T08:54:12Z","event":"kms:DecryptDenied","resource":"proxy-keystore-canary-1","principal":"serviceAccount:proxy-keystore-canary@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com","key":"projects/redwood-prod/locations/europe-west1/keyRings/keystore-prod/cryptoKeys/keystore-key","reason":"missing iam role roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter"}
```

This is exact behavior we expect for mismatched permissions.
Omar (DevOps): I'll stage the temporary IAM binding for canary and post the audit link + terraform diff in the thread. Anyone want to own the runbook update?
Priya (Oncall): I got runbook.
Ralph (Dev): I'll finish the SA scan and open PRs to use the new alias names.
Jess (SRE): I'll add an automation to pause the rollout when the metric crosses the threshold and tie it to the deployment pipeline.
Anna (Security): Action items (short):
- Omar: stage temporary IAM binding for canary & post audit link
- Priya: runbook update + exact gcloud snippets and alert thresholds
- Ralph: scan services and open PRs for alias migration
- Jess: dashboard thresholds + deployment pause automation

Please ack if you're taking ownership. :thumbsup:
